sentences.text: ----Respondent For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Awar Dan Ujjwal
For Respondent(s) : Mr. Sharwan Singh Rathore, Dy.GA.
HON'BLE
MR. JUSTICE KULDEEP MATHUR Order 12/11/2024 1.

This application for bail under Section 439 Cr.P.C. (483 BNSS) has been filed by the petitioner who has been arrested in connection with F.I.R. No.248/2023, registered at Police Station Sendra,
District Beawar, for offences under Sections 366, 376 & 506 of IPC.
2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Public Prosecutor.
Perused the material available on record.

3. As per the prosecution, learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that on 19.12.2023, the prosecutrix- 'P' was subjected to forcible sexual assault- rape by the present petitioner on a knife point.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner contended that the statements of the prosecutrix- 'P' have already been recorded before the competent criminal Court on 21.10.2024 as PW.2 and [2024:RJ-JD:45560] (2 of 3) [CRLMB-6810/2024
] therefore, now there is no apprehension of the petitioner influencing her or tampering with the evidence.

entities.text: Praveen Singh vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:45560)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Drawing attention of the Court towards the statements of the prosecutrix- 'P' (PW.2), learned counsel submitted that the prosecutrix- 'P' in her statements has admitted that had she shouted for help at the place of incident i.e. house of the Joravar Singh, the shout could be heard by the residents of the nearby areas.
However, there is nothing on record to indicate that the prosecutrix- 'P' made any attempt to seek help at the time when the alleged incident took place.
Further, the prosecutrix- 'P' has admitted of not having received any internal or external injury on her body.

6. Lastly, learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner who is aged about 27 years,
is in judicial custody since 21.12.2023 and the trial of the case will take sufficiently long time,
therefore, the benefit of bail should be granted to the accused-petitioner.
7.
Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor has vehemently opposed the bail application.

8. Having considered the rival submissions, facts and circumstances of the case and after perusing the statements of the prosecutrix- 'P' recorded before the competent criminal Court as PW.2, this Court prima facie finds that the statements of the prosecutrix- 'P' have already been recorded before the competent criminal Court and therefore, now there is no apprehension of the petitioner influencing the prosecutrix- 'P' or tampering with the evidence.

This Court also finds that the prosecution has not shown [2024:RJ-JD:45560] (3 of 3) [CRLMB-6810/2024] any apprehension of the petitioner influencing the remaining prosecution witnesses or fleeing away from justice, in case,
he is enlarged on bail.
Thus, without expressing any opinion on merits/ demerits of the case, this Court is inclined to enlarge the petitioner on bail.
9. Consequently, the bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. (483 BNSS) is allowed.

It is ordered that the accused-petitioner- Praveen Singh S/o Moti Singh, arrested in connection with F.I.R.
No.248/2023, registered at Police Station Sendra, District Beawar, shall be released on bail, if not wanted in any other case, provided he furnishes a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- and two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each, to the satisfaction of learned trial Court, for his appearance before that Court on each & every date of hearing and whenever called upon to do so till completion of the trial.

(KULDEEP MATHUR),J 12-himanshu/-
